concepts.title: Income
concepts.definition: All the money coming in during a month.
concepts.tip: Plan with the amount you are sure to receive, not the amount you hope for.

concepts.title: Fixed expenses
concepts.definition: Costs that stay the same every month and are hard to skip.
concepts.tip: Pay these first, right after your income arrives.

concepts.title: Variable expenses
concepts.definition: Costs that change from month to month depending on your choices.
concepts.tip: This is where most overspending happens, so track these closely.

concepts.title: Needs
concepts.definition: Things you must pay for to live, study and stay safe.
concepts.tip: A need can still be bought cheaply: used books count too.

concepts.title: Wants
concepts.definition: Things that make life more fun or comfortable but can wait.
concepts.tip: Wants are fine. Give them a set limit instead of cutting them out.

concepts.title: Savings
concepts.definition: Money you keep aside for goals and emergencies.
concepts.tip: Treat savings as a bill you pay yourself every month.

sampleBudget.title: Ayesha's month: a first-year student living in a hostel

quiz.question: Monthly hostel rent is an example of which kind of expense?
quiz.explanation: Rent is the same amount every month, so it is a fixed expense.

quiz.question: Your grocery bill was $80 last month and $110 this month. What kind of expense is it?
quiz.explanation: The amount changes month to month, which makes it a variable expense.

quiz.question: When is the best time to move money into savings?
options: At the end of the month, if anything is left
Only when you get a bonus
quiz.explanation: Saving first, before spending, makes the habit automatic instead of optional.
